summary: Telegram-controlled remote shell and filesystem exfiltration in infogram-bot
details: The package implements a Telegram bot that turns the installer's host into a remotely controllable shell. Message text received from Telegram users is dispatched by handlers.t to core.run_cmd, which invokes subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True,...), giving anyone with the bot token and an owner-listed Telegram ID full shell execution on the host running the bot. Additional Telegram commands read installer-side data and send it back over the same channel: `.printenv` returns the full os.environ, `take <file>` and `take all` upload arbitrary files via reply_document, `get all` builds a split zip archive of the current working tree and uploads it, and `.grep` scans files and environment variables for matches and returns hits. Owner-ID gating restricts who can invoke the commands but does not change the network-to-shell dataflow. pyproject.toml also ships with placeholder author metadata ("Aapka Naam" / you@example.com) and a Homepage of https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/infogram, indicating unattributed publication alongside the remote-shell payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
